newsitem.title: UK: YEAREND-Australia stocks set for growth in 97.
newsitem.headline: YEAREND-Australia stocks set for growth in 97.

text.p: Australian shares are expected to show solid and strengthening growth during 1997, a Reuters survey of the outlook for the world's top bourses shows.

The All Ordinaries index should grow by around eight percent to end 1997 at around 2,540 points, the survey showed, with strong earnings growth offsetting any downward pressure from a correction in U.S. shares.
The index received a strong kick on Wednesday after the Reserve Bank of Australia cut official cash rates by 0.5 percent to 6.0 percent, citing an improved inflation outlook.
Following are a selection of views on next year's performance of the Australian share market:
MARCUS TUCK, CHIEF ECONOMIST HSBC JAMES CAPEL

"We think the global bull market for equities is still intact. It seems to us that globally and in Australia we're going to be in a trend-growth, low-inflation environment which should hopefully mean that interest rates can stay fairly low."
JOHN BANOS, DIRECTOR AND HEAD OF STRATEGY, MCINTOSH AND CO

"Even if we do get a correction, the fundamentals for the market are really good in the sense that we're looking for continued growth in the next year or two. Inflation will be manageable so the fundamentals for equities are reasonably all right. It's just that prices have gone a bit too high."
BRUCE HOCKMAN, ECONOMIST AND EQUITIES STRATEGIST, BAIN & CO

"It's all a matter of timing. If we see the expected downturn in the United States come before the upturn in our resources sector, then it's going to look ugly. But if as we expect the resources upturn comes before or at the same time as the Dow selloff, then we will be all right."
